subject: Custody & key model options — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Costa <security@finledger.com>; Michael Oduro <cto@finledger.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Custody & key model options — post-call recap and asks

Thanks again for the call earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and the items we committed to follow up on: 

Summary of requirements I heard from FinLedger:
- Data residency: EU (primary region eu-west-1 / Ireland).
- PII handling: treat direct identifiers as sensitive; prefer tokenization/hashing before longer-term storage.
- Retention: transaction-level logs retained 7 years; aggregated metrics shorter (90 days).
- Logging: need audit logs from inference requests (request id, model, route, timestamp, requester id) forwarded to your Splunk instance.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+ mandatory; at-rest encryption required with customer-managed key (CMEK) and HSM backing if possible.

Options we outlined on the call (high-level):
1) BYOK via AWS KMS + CloudHSM (recommended for customers who need key custody and HSM root).
2) Redwood-managed keys with dual-control and export-proof key handling (faster onboarding, lower ops footprint).
3) Hybrid: Customer KMS for primary keys, Redwood KMS for ephemeral session keys with clear separation of roles and audit trail.

Attachments: I attached our KMS options brief (redwood_kms_options.pdf) and the KMS integration playbook for your infra team.

Asks / next steps I have for FinLedger: 
- Confirm whether BYOK with HSM (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM) is a hard requirement, or if Redwood-managed keys with restricted export controls would be acceptable for a POC.
- Confirm the Splunk endpoint type (HEC token or syslog over TLS) and the team we should coordinate with for log forwarding.
- Share any specific compliance artifacts you need for procurement (SOC2 report, architecture diagram, KMS audit expectations).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- Technical workshop (60 min) with your infra + security + our security/infra engineers to walk the KMS/HSM integration patterns and logging design. Calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/markus/tech-workshop
- Share SOC2 Type II and architecture diagram (will attach in follow-up).

If you can confirm the three asks above we’ll lock the scope for the workshop and bring the right infra folks.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_kms_options.pdf, kms-integration-playbook.odt
From: Ana Costa <security@finledger.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Oduro <cto@finledger.com>, procurement@finledger.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Custody & key model options — post-call recap and asks

Markus / team,

Thanks for the clear recap — confirms what we discussed. A few clarifications and answers from FinLedger Security: 

1) Key custody: CMEK with HSM is a requirement for production. We operate under strict custody policies — keys must be in an HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM or equivalent). We prefer CloudHSM in eu-west-1 for initial POC.

2) Data residency: yes, all production inference and logs must remain in the eu-west-1 region. For the POC, a test environment in eu-west-1 is acceptable.

3) Logging & retention: we need audit logs (detailed request-level logs) forwarded to our Splunk HEC (token-based ingestion) and retained in our environment for 7 years. We will require assurance that request payloads flagged as PII are redacted before forwarding.

4) Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+; at-rest encrypted with customer keys (AES-256) managed through KMS. We will need to see an architecture diagram showing where keys live and who has access.

5) Compliance artifacts: please send SOC2 Type II and any penetration test summaries you can share. I've attached the security questionnaire we started filling out (finledger_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf).

A couple of practical asks for the workshop: please include your infra engineer who owns the KMS integration and your security lead who can speak to key rotation and audit trails. We will bring our infra and Splunk admin. 

Thanks — happy to do the workshop next week if you have availability.

Best,
Ana Costa
Head of Security, FinLedger
security@finledger.com

Attachment: finledger_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Costa <security@finledger.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Oduro <cto@finledger.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody & key model options — post-call recap and asks

Ana — perfect, thanks for the detail and for the completed questionnaire. Quick notes based on your answers and proposed path forward: 

Short path options for POC / production:
- POC (recommended): provision a Private deployment in eu-west-1 with BYOK via AWS KMS backed by CloudHSM. This gives you direct custody, and we can demonstrate key rotation, split-access controls, and end-to-end audit logs.
- Faster POC alternative: Redwood-managed keys with strict access controls and an audit trail. We can lock export and provide attestation; lower ops for FinLedger but does not satisfy a hard HSM requirement.

Logging & forwarding: we can stream request-level audit logs to your Splunk HEC over TLS with token auth. We’ll add a configurable redaction pipeline so any PII fields you flag are removed before forwarding. Implementation options: forwarding from the runtime (low-latency) or from a log aggregator in your VPC (more control).

Artifacts we will provide ahead of the workshop:
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted where needed)
- Architecture diagram showing KMS placement, key lifecycle, and where audit logs are collected/forwarded
- KMS integration playbook (attached) with sample CloudFormation snippets for KMS grants and CloudHSM setup

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Schedule the 60 minute technical workshop (please use the calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/markus/tech-workshop). Suggested attendees: your infra lead, Splunk admin, CISO/security, our infra engineer (Soong), and our security lead (Soojin).
2) During the workshop we’ll validate the CloudHSM flow, redaction rules, and retention configuration for Splunk.
3) Post-workshop: we’ll provide a test env in eu-west-1 with the HSM-BYOK encryption profile and a short runbook for log forwarding.

I’ll have Soojin follow up with a proposed agenda and internal owners for each action. Looking good — happy to lock time next week.

—
Markus

Attachments: kms-integration-playbook.odt, redwood_kms_options.pdf
